answer: Rule: every name that joins in a given week shares one fixed newcomer vote, split evenly. An honest agent selling ferrous scrap that joins during a plume of sign-ups gets a thinner slice and waits longer to matter. The loss is worth it: a forger who pours a thousand names into one week adds nothing to that vote and leaves each name a crumb, while a tundra survey agent arriving in a quiet week keeps its full share.
